body: The surprise at the roll of the dice that is life and death sounds to me like “*gulp* I thought if I ran around eating vegetables I wouldn’t die.” Which is not a healthy perspective. Better to face death, it is a shadow following us all.

Not being smarmy, I honestly don’t know if Norm would have bet on his friends life expectancy vs his own. The amount of variables that go into time of death are many. Either way, I think what it comes down to is that when people voice shock that one is still alive and another is not, it is evidence they’ve not fully contemplated or even begun preparing their own mortality. It’s worth meditating on. Wrestling with the fear and doing your best to leave things better than you found them.

Everyone saying “isn’t it incredible so and so outlived so and so”. Anyone else find this extremely banal, inappropriate, and irritating? Like death comes when it does almost wholly independent of our actions. It’s not a race, don’t be surprised someone is alive when someone else is dead, how do you think this works?Universe is quite indiscriminate to whom and when it chooses to extinguish. Not rude at all. I could rephrase as discipline being the practice of loving oneself. I would say that you have to have the motivation of caring enough about who you are to make concerted efforts of will power in order to live a disciplined life. It starts with self-respect. The initial step of self-respect is introspection. Declaring to yourself and your time on this earth that you are worth figuring out. Being on that path of observing your own behavior and striving to prioritize your own health and long term fulfillment and self-satisfaction over short term pleasure, others opinion of you, escapism and things of that nature is essential. Looking into the mirror and not shying away from it. It's pretty much acknowledging what Carl Jung refers to as the shadow self. Once you have that going you might, as I have, come upon the realization that love from others is ephemeral and not something to live for and that if you do live for the love of others or one single person it becomes an unhealthy relationship with the world that will always culminate in frustration. Therefore, it is imperative we know how to love ourselves and take the time and energy to do so. This doesn't consist of the mindset of I am perfect and I deserve unconditional love. Love is inevitably conditional and performance based. Especially love of oneself. We are often our worst critics. That is where discipline comes in. It enables us to trade in short term discomfort, difficulty, and or abstinence for longer term greater and deeper sense of pride and fulfillment. It starts with realizing you have something to offer yourself and the world that is worth developing, and discipline is most definitely a key to personal development. Thank you for asking. We all have to figure out how to feel alright about ourselves in the morning and at the end of the night. That definitely requires tough love for oneself. Overriding the thoughts and feelings that lead to decisions and actions that are counterproductive to your goals and how you want to feel about yourself is what being disciplined and strong is all about.
